source.quote: But there is one more mining related farm that I did want to test. So down by the Grimsilt Digite area, there are tempered war golems. And these are interesting because once you kill them, you can actually mine them. They don't drop a lot, but consistently they give either one mythal ore or one thorium ore. Basically, it's golem skinning. And if we didn't have Swamp of Soros, this would be one of our only ways to consistently get Thorium. And the golems spawn in a crescent around the dig site. And they do hypers spawn. So, naturally, we have to test it. They also have a blue POE on their table, Blanchard's Stout, which sounds like a good ale, but it's actually a cool looking mace with a 0.03% drop rate. However, it's only worth about 4,000 gold, which would be cool to get, but it's definitely not worth farming 10 hours for. There's also a couple Mythil nodes that spawn in the same area. So, if it's not too far away, I'm going to go ahead and grab these during the golem skinning. And after one full hour farming here, here's the results. I pulled in 228 Myithil ore, 188 Thorium ore, 21 rough stone, two true silver, and about 100 gold of vendor trash, which is pretty much just random gray rocks, which puts the farm at a total gold per hour of 3,800. I didn't get any notable BOE's dropping during this hour of testing, but it's still pretty respectable. And notably, it actually beats the skinning farm in the zone by a few hundred gold per hour.

source.quote: So some very interesting possibilities coming up. And speaking of the randomizer and some classic goldie farms, the next one I'm both excited and a little bit nervous for because well, we've got ourselves another potential pickpocket farm. All the dark iron dwarves, excavators, and cultists here are actually pickpocketable. And heading down into the mines, the slave workers can be pickpocketed as well. And after looking into the loot tables, I don't know whether to be happy or a little worried to say it. They have junk boxes. Yeah, so far junk boxes haven't exactly been kind to Goldie as a reliable gold per hour farm. They're really, really, really a bad bet. But we can always spend a couple hours pickpocketing them to hopefully get something good because what if this time they had Too's Blazing Long Sword? I mean, it'd be worth it then. So, I guess it's time to set off and pickpocket 100 locked junk boxes for another opening. Luckily, we do still have mining. And the highest density of pickpocketable mobs is in the slag pit between the slave workers and the foremen. And there there's also a good amount of myithil ore. So, while I'm doing laps pickpocketing, I can also mine some myithil. That way, even if we go completely dry on the boxes, there's still at least some consistent gold coming in from the ore. On top of that, the slave workers are actually dropping a pretty non-negligible amount of magewave cloth. It doesn't sell for a ton. But on Goldie, where we can't buy cloth off the auction house, stockpiling on this for future tailoring is actually pretty helpful. And aside from heading outside the mines every hour or so for a bit of fresh air, there isn't much else to say about the grind itself, except for one thing. Up top, the dark iron steammiths were pickpocketing and killing actually have a pretty notable drop on their loot tables. The pattern for the shadow weave mask, a BOE tailoring recipe. The pattern itself has a value of about 5,000 to 10,000 gold. And the mask itself also sells for around 2,000 gold with a pretty juicy sale rate. And that's because the Shadowwave mask is used partway through the scavenger hunt for the Lucid Nightmare mount. It's required and most guides actually recommend just buying the mask off the auction house before starting these steps, which keeps the demand for sales pretty steady. And even though the recipe is a 1.7% drop rate, I ended up with eight of these while farming the lock boxes. Yeah, a lot of dwarves were taken out. So, I'll just try to sell a few of the patterns on the auction house as patterns, but I am going to hold on to a couple for the next time I level tailoring. Having some shadowy masks on the auction house definitely wouldn't hurt. Anyways, after about 3 and 1 half hours of pickpocketing, we once again have 100 junk boxes in the inventory. So the only thing next is to carefully lockpick all of them and then with fingers crossed open them hoping once again for a t-boo blazing long sword or at least something yet again only trash. So aside from the myith mythil ore the patterns the mage weave and the regular mob loot these lock boxes are worth about two gold per hour and a total waste of time but you never know they're a bit of an RNG lottery. Okay, so with that all wrapped up in game, the midnight pre- patch has actually just hit the servers.

source.quote: And after a little bit of downtime, we're actually online and playing, which has a few new changes. First off, there was a massive stat squish. But since Goldie is currently the max level, level 80 in vanilla zones, this doesn't really affect him all that much. What does matter though is the talent rework. A lot of classes in retail got reworked and from a gold making perspective, outlaw rogues just got buffed and almost all of it comes down to movement speed. So check this out. In the base rogue tree, there's a talent called fleetfooted which gives a flat 15% move speed. From what I can tell, this applies to both run speed and mount speed. On top of that, there's Shadowrunner, which gives 20% movement speed while stealththed. So right there, there's already a 35% move speed buff as a rogue, but those were already there before the patch. And moving into the outlaw tree, there's a new talent, hit and run, which adds another 15% movement speed to the base. So while stealththed, Goldie is sitting at 50% base movement speed increased. And that's not even the end of it. Sprint was also buffed with a talent, both for duration plus 4 seconds, and speed increase from 70% to 100% bonus. And it doesn't even end there. source.quote: And honestly, that's kind of nice because it frees Goldie up to just camp mining while we're in the Syrian gorge and to have an extra professional slot that's kind of flex without worrying too much about dropping herbalism. Now, at this point, while doing some farming, I've come across most of Seiring Gorge's rare spawns. There are a handful of them, but from what I can tell, none of them have a major ticket unique transmunk item on their loot tables. They do still drop green bees in the 500 gold to 2500 gold range, so they're worth killing when you pass them on a flight or a farming route. But in terms of actively camping rare timers, that doesn't seem like a super profitable angle here in Searing Gorge. From what we do have though, this zone is absolutely solid for mining. And since we're flying around, we're definitely taking them out as we go. On top of that, we have unlocked a few weekly raids added to the rotation. I touched on them briefly earlier in the video, but the two new ones are Blackwing Layer and Blackwing Descent. And after doing some runs, both of them have their own interesting angles. Blackwing Layer in particular is one where it can be very helpful to bring 300 skinning, and that's because of Chromagus. While there are other skinnable mobs in the raid that give some trade goods, Chromagus is the only reliable source of blue dragon scales in the entire game. The only other source are two rare spawns in Winter Spring that have a super low drop chance when skinning. And because blue dragon scales are used in some rare recipes, they hold pretty strong value, often hovering around 500 to 600 gold each. And you usually get one to three per skin attempt on Chromagus, which does add up over time if you're running the raid weekly. So, when at all possible on Goldie, I'm power leveling up, skinning 1 to 300, usually through Sunken Temple or now the Incendosaur Farm, and then doing Blackwing Lair. It just adds a little bit of gold to the pouches. Then there's Blackwing Descent.
